evidence: Quint. 10.7.27: studendum est semper et ubīque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “wherever it be”, and so “everywhere”. Cicero’s phrase for “everyone everywhere” is omnēs quī ubīque sunt (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: all over, here and there, in every direction
evidence: Ov. F. 3.525–526: viridēs passim disjecta per herbās
Caes. BC 2.38: nūllīs ōrdinibus passim cōnsēderant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Scattered “hither and thither”, often “at random”, without order (Lewis & Short); see throughout.

evidence: Caes. BG 3.1: vīcus altissimīs montibus undique continētur (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.22: ut undique ūnō tempore in hostēs impetus fieret (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First “from all sides” (undique concurritur, people run together from everywhere, Cicero), then “on every side, all round”, and “in every respect” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: he who is everywhere is nowhere

phrases.latin: cāsus ubīque valet; semper tibi pendeat hāmus: quō minimē crēdās gurgite, piscis erit
phrases.english: chance is strong everywhere; keep your hook always hanging: in the pool where you least expect it there will be a fish

phrases.latin: aut Epicūrus, quid sit voluptās, aut omnēs mortālēs quī ubīque sunt nesciunt
phrases.english: either Epicurus does not know what pleasure is, or all mortals everywhere do not
the village is shut in on every side by very high mountains

short-que.html: Ov. Met. 1.214, longa mora est, quantum noxae sit ubīque repertum (quoted by Lewis & Short): the fifth foot, -bīque re-, is a dactyl. The -que is the generalising enclitic, short as in undique (Lewis & Short undĭquĕ).

sources: Lewis & Short: ubique · Lewis & Short: passim · Lewis & Short: undique
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-ovidius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
